messages:
sam: Jane-cust opened a ticket: JSON mode output breaks when invoice notes include a form-feed (U+000C). They sent a minimal curl repro:

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"gptx-code","mode":"json","prompt":"generate invoice"}'
```

Response body (snippet they observed):

```
{"invoice_id":"inv_123","notes":"Payment duePlease contact billing"}
```

Their client fails with: "Unexpected control character at line 1 column 42" when calling JSON.parse.

leah: Were they streaming the response? Which SDK / client version? Any stack traces from the client?

mike: I repro'd this locally with node fetch + streaming. The runtime is sometimes splitting the Unicode escape across chunks: one chunk ends with a backslash and the next chunk starts with "u000c". The client sees a literal 0x0C form-feed, so JSON.parse throws.

sam: This is blocking their billing pipeline — invoices can't be parsed. Need mitigation ASAP.

leah: Short-term workaround: ask them to set streaming=false or add a header to enable server-side escaping. Also we can enable the SDK flag `atomic_json_writes:true` if available. I'll prepare a temporary flag to escape control characters on the server for affected customers.

support-bot: Filed internal incident INC-2026: https://internal.redwood.ai/incidents/INC-2026

mike: Minimal repro I used (Node):

```js
const res = await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers, body });
const reader = res.body.getReader();
let buf = '';
while (true) {
  const { value, done } = await reader.read();
  if (done) break;
  buf += new TextDecoder().decode(value);
}
console.log(buf); // sometimes contains a raw form-feed 0x0C
```

Observed chunk sequence: `{"invoice_id":"inv_123","notes":"Payment due\` then next chunk `u000cPlease contact billing"}` — notice the split of the escape.

leah: Root cause confirmed: chunk-boundary can split a `\uXXXX` escape. Fix plan: (1) ensure serializer never emits a trailing backslash as the final byte of a chunk for JSON mode, (2) add server-side control-char escaping as an interim mitigation, (3) add unit tests that fuzz split-escape boundaries.

sam: Can we flip on a per-customer flag to escape control chars until the runtime patch ships?

leah: Yes. I'll open a PR and enable `json_escape_controlchars=true` for jane-cust. ETA ~2h. For now, ask customer to retry with header `x-redwood-json-escape: on` or set streaming=false.

jane-cust: Tried header + same request, parsing succeeds now. Thanks :tada:

mike: :thumbsup: We'll ship the permanent fix in next runtime release and keep the incident open until then.
